subject.title: gateway tool not available to external-provider agent sessions

question: Should explicitly allowlisted `gateway` remain available to external-provider agent sessions, or should external providers be intentionally blocked from this control-plane tool?
rationale: Current source looks like explicit allowlisting is intended to work, but `gateway` can read and mutate configuration and restart services, so changing external-provider exposure needs a maintainer security-boundary decision before automation repairs it.

options.title: Preserve explicit allowlisting
options.body: Treat the report as a bug, reproduce the xAI/Grok path, and fix the shared filtering path while keeping gateway authorization checks intact.

options.title: Restrict external providers
options.body: Document and enforce that external-provider sessions cannot receive `gateway`, even when explicitly allowlisted, and provide a clear diagnostic message.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a Windows/xAI/Grok live repro shows whether current main still drops the tool.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit allowlisting
recommendation.body: Treat the report as a bug, reproduce the xAI/Grok path, and fix the shared filtering path while keeping gateway authorization checks intact.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the effective-inventory gateway method and provider-aware tool inventory surface that their history appears to have introduced.
